finding.classification: new source-derived conditional planner projection mismatch; no observed gameplay state or rendering
finding.first_contract: Native case-site start stores the outbound active leg, its forecast camp intervals and elapsed time only. The camp template treats a case-site destination as a round trip, passes outbound-plus-return movement total to the planner and synthesizes persisted movement up to twice the outbound duration inside the stored outbound elapsed time. The client positions both the quest turnaround and the return End on this mixed representation.
finding.conditions: An active journey to a case site reaches camp with a remaining walking interval and its camp page receives a stored journey. For outbound movement A, a synthetic trailing walking interval ending at 2A is compressed into the native outbound-only elapsed interval; if an independently stored return B differs from A, another field instead says A+B. Client interpolation may place the quest/return markers before the corresponding active-leg arrival. This is symbolic source reasoning, not an observed user session, runtime, actual asymmetric route, or claim the stored authority moves a character incorrectly.
finding.safeguards: Native case-site route admission validates outgoing and independently planned return; a later return starts its own active journey. Map pre-departure round-trip forecasting is a separate intended view. Preserve camp status, actual-versus-forecast boundaries and correct duration authority.
finding.relationship: q1002 records a broader return-route and timing policy question; old strategic calendar assessment previously read travel.rs:455–548 at c100 but did not establish this active-leg-to-display mismatch. Current 059 identities and prior assessments searched without exact alias found. The neighboring mirrored terrain case is a distinct transformation in the same planner family.
finding.future_repair_direction: After the audit gate, define whether the camp timeline represents the actual active leg or a separate full round-trip projection; compute movement, elapsed, return route and markers coherently from the same declared authority, including independently timed return legs.

finding.classification: current source finding refining existing 059 q552; distinct first failure subject to central alias reconciliation
finding.title: One failed subject request prevents all wheels in the refresh from applying
finding.trace: Refresh awaits Promise.all before rendering any wheel. strategicBackgroundFetch calls strategicFetch, which throws on every non-OK response before the response.ok fallback can execute. The condition route returns 401, 404, or 403 for authentication/observation/frontier/party/location failures. One rejection therefore causes the aggregate await to reject and none of that refresh's successful wheel results are applied; independent fetches may continue. A 200 JSON null separately renders the individual unavailable state, including when the condition query fails or returns no row.
finding.conditions: Requires a refresh containing at least one failed request and at least one wheel. No actual network failure, rendered outcome or user data was observed. Wheels can remain loading or retain their previously rendered value; no claim that every underlying request fails. When null is rendered, the previous data-condition-status attribute is not cleared, but no red ring or visual consequence is claimed without rendering evidence.
finding.future_repair_direction: Resolve results per subject, preserving authorized observation and individual unknown/error states, without exposing restricted data; keep newer-generation freshness and cancel semantics explicit. Define distinct missing versus backend failure only after tracing producer/error policy.
relationships: 059 q552 Q-L11-166d8c725fa6521a3142 explicitly requested availability, producer and encumbrance reconciliation. READ-L11-399 historically recorded that exceptions retain the earlier wheel until global reporting; this is a newly assessed precise Promise.all/fetch/403 trace, not a claim the historical observation was novel or already closed.

finding.classification: new bounded current source finding; related to 059 q547 without asserting exact alias

Clicking another evidence item while that request is pending changes selectedId and details, but completion unconditionally replaces the returned item and calls selectEvidence(updated, button), restoring the older item and its description/conversation. The reducer keys an exact action receipt by action ID/actor/evidence/topic and the underlying attempt by actor/evidence/topic; already attempted results are reused, with successful results potentially augmented by newly learned lore.

A per-click action ID is not by itself proof of a duplicate inspection attempt or universal exactly-once contract. The request is not bound to the mount signal, but detached references do not by themselves prove stale mutation of a live page.
finding.future_repair_direction: Bind view publication to its originating selection and mount identity while separately retaining permitted authoritative result/cache updates. Trace current mount replacement and decide stale error reporting independently of backend action receipt guarantees.
relationships: 059 q547 Q-L11-d405c7e56b251cc465c6 already posed physical evidence mount lifetime, action IDs and native receipt questions without adjudicating first failure. finding.classification: new current source finding, qualifying the historical wrapper-only assessment; actual retry failure unproven
finding.title: The errantry retry helper cannot observe the HTTP statuses it handles
finding.trace: createRetriableAction retains its action ID after failures except 409/422, where it intends to clear it. Its request wrapper would attach error.status for non-OK responses, but strategicFetch throws a plain Error first, so that wrapper's non-OK branch cannot execute. The current errantry route maps every DB call error to 422; a failed call reaches the retry helper without numeric status and retains its previous ID. The native owner checks exact session/action receipt first, confirms actor and current case/contract, and otherwise validates live dialogue presence, issuer and materialization before creating a receipt.
finding.conditions: Requires an acceptance request returning a non-OK response, particularly the reachable 422 mapping. Retention is a source-proven mismatch with the helper's explicit branch, not proof that a later retry fails, mutates twice, or needs a fresh ID: a failed request lacking an existing receipt may later succeed with the same ID, and exact lost-response retries benefit from stable identity. The route also combines all DB failures as 422, so blindly resetting all such failures could lose a needed replay identity. No network, reducer or browser execution occurred.
finding.future_repair_direction: Preserve structured status/cause at the fetch boundary and define an authority-aware distinction between definitive rejection and ambiguous delivery, coordinating action identity and native receipt reuse. Preserve authorized actor/presence checks and exact replay semantics.
relationships: READ-L12-811 historical Lens12 summary described the wrapper as retaining numeric status and the helper clearing 409/422. That is a historical summary of its scoped inspection; this separately registered fetch boundary contradicts the assumed actual call chain at 95e and must be attached as a qualification, not rewritten into its original record or attributed to its reviewer. ROOT-ADMISSION03-REG-040 historically materialized helper lines 4–72 and 100–108 only; see older 774 attribution below.

finding.trace: The script keys buys by catalog item and sales by inventory row, preserves separate lists on submission, yet preview first nets quantities by catalog item and chooses one buy price or the first matching sale-row price. The source-only centered-dialog CSS did not reveal a full-screen backdrop in these bounded rules, but real user interaction, actual stock/data, full navigation/focus routing, currency rounding, successful transaction and UI display remain unverified. finding.classification: conditional source-level cache availability question; no observed failure or supported browser reachability established
finding.first_contract: When IndexedDB is enabled, cache.get computes SHA-256 for the job address before the guarded storage transaction. A rejection/throw from that digest, or from checksum digest on an existing record, escapes cache.get; coordinator resolveJob does not catch it, the pool closes and rethrows, and preparation is cancelled rather than regenerating as an optional-cache miss.
finding.conditions: The cache is enabled and a subsequent crypto.subtle.digest invocation for a job key or existing stored checksum throws or rejects, despite successful startup. Normal renderer startup already requires an initial SHA-256 digest of the Wasm binary, so a browser wholly lacking crypto.subtle fails earlier and is not an established ordinary path to this cache case. Actual supported browser API, intermittent platform failure, runtime reuse and alternate callers are uninspected; no crypto fault or failed scene was observed.
finding.safeguards: Missing IndexedDB, blocked open and transaction timeouts use explicit cache-unavailable/miss paths; malformed product decoding is evicted only for specific Rust product errors. Writes are deferred and failure reported separately, not on this lookup path. Prior SHA-256 over stored bytes checks integrity but is not authentication.
finding.relationship: q1899 is the broader original product-address/cache boundary obligation; prior worker-trust and 774 CONT07-560/SEGOVB-INITIAL04-581 summaries are related but do not establish this particular digest-rejection first cut. The old operations summary that optional-cache failure does not gate readiness did not document this escaping pre-transaction call; preserve that as an older qualified summary, not a retroactive historical finding. Central decides final aliases and whether this supported-failure policy is actionable.
finding.future_repair_direction: After the audit gate, decide the browser crypto/readiness contract and distinguish optional-cache-only digest failures from mandatory Wasm product or dependency failures; preserve typed invalid-product eviction and authoritative Rust admission.

finding.title: A failed resident-place request can leave an incomplete roster eligible for scene readiness
finding.trace: On entering a new settlement, mount clears roster and calls preload for the set of places. preload awaits Promise.all; any rejected place request discards all successful entries, sets rosterPending false and reports a scene failure, but retains no roster-error/incomplete flag. The catch does not itself schedule a new sync. On a subsequent sync, people may be supplied from the current DOM and a scene can be prepared with the partial/empty roster. Browser readiness checks !rosterPending but no roster-error flag; native readiness tests the people actually supplied in that view, not an independent complete roster.
finding.conditions: Requires a failed place request, later scheduling, enough remaining DOM/current data to prepare a scene, and all other native asset/equipment/revision readiness conditions to succeed. The view may contain some DOM people, so this does not assert a completely empty scene or that every request failed. A later live update can refresh the roster. No real request failure, missing resident, readiness transition or UI was observed.
finding.future_repair_direction: Retain roster observation completeness and per-place failures separately from valid empty results, and gate or clearly qualify the view readiness according to policy. Keep successful authorized place data and generation guards, avoiding disclosure beyond existing route authority.

finding.title: Prepared scene state is published without waiting for command queue acceptance
finding.trace: After worker preparation and an abort check, load calls install synchronously, sets residentLocation and publishes prepared. The install callback calls command, which schedules wasm_command in a Promise and catches/logs rejection; load neither awaits nor receives that rejection, so its synchronous catch cannot cancel a ticket for an asynchronous queue failure. wasm_command returns the native queue_json Result and serde decode or queue lock can fail. finding.title: Changing the place set without changing location does not rebuild retained venues
finding.trace: The browser derives its current places from nav DOM but reuses a prepared scene by location. Native retain_scene prepares venues only when the location differs or root is missing and stores next_place as the initial view length. Native status requires next_place to equal current view.places.len(); retain_people skips a person whose place is absent from the old venue map. Thus, if a retained same-location nav changes place count, this particular readiness conjunct remains false until the root/location is reset; with a same-count substitution, the new place can remain missing from the old map even though the count matches. Scene assets also capture current official minute and operator profile, whose freshness is not in the location key.
finding.conditions: Requires an admitted same-location place-set update and a retained root with the same location. Normal service/DOM update reachability, whether scene time and profile must refresh, and whether another lifecycle resets the root first remain unproven. No observed missing person, stuck scene, data race or visual rendering is claimed.
finding.future_repair_direction: Define the identity/version of the generated scene and venue set and rebuild or incrementally reconcile the native venue map when material inputs change, preserving intentional cached products, route authority, cancellation and live tactical boundary.
